items.title: Projecta
items.text:
Projecta helps to explore data and medical images: load a file, a table or an exam, and the application summarizes it, shows it in 2D and 3D, measures it.

Download for Windows The online dashboard The desktop app

  • Load data: a file (CSV, Excel, Parquet…), a table of a database, a web link, S3 or SFTP.
  • Explore and export: the overview, the columns, the export.
  • Visualize: PCA, t-SNE or UMAP projections in 2D and 3D, empty cells filled.
  • Medical imaging: DICOM, NIfTI or PACS; three planes, measurements, follow-up, report.
  • Assistant: answers and proposals about the open screen; you decide.
  • Workspaces: your datasets, your settings, your history, per project.

items.title: The screen
items.text:
1. Choose data: a file, a table, a remote server.
  2. Three ways to start: a file, a database table, medical images.
  3. The open workspace; a click shows the others.
  4. Assistant: the panel of questions and proposals.
  5. This guide (the book).
  6. Your account: profile, language, settings, notifications, what’s new.
Area Content Top bar side menu, workspace, Assistant, this guide, account Side menu Choose data; ANALYSIS: Home, Overview (and Columns), Visualizations; IMAGING: Studies, Viewer, Compare, Report; recent datasets Centre the chosen screen Right panel the assistant, when open

The side menu is hidden: the page takes all the room. The pointer on the button left of the logo shows it over the page, without moving it, as long as it stays on the button or the menu (as in the Claude application). A click on this button keeps it open, another hides it; the choice is kept in the browser.

items.title: On a tablet and a phone
items.text:
The online dashboard also opens on a tablet: everything is there, the menu hidden (the button top left shows it), buttons the size of a finger, the table scrolling in its card. On a phone, it is for looking: a bar at the bottom (Home, Overview, Studies, Assistant), your recent datasets and studies, the overview and its visualization in two tabs, one view at a time, and the viewer plane by plane (Axial, Coronal, Sagittal, 3D). Loading a file, connecting to a database, segmenting or writing a report are done on a computer or a tablet. A shared study also opens on a phone.

The sign-in pages follow: on a tablet in landscape, Projecta on the left and the form on the right; on a phone, one column, and creating an account starts with Google and GitHub. The fields keep their name above them, Google and GitHub show theirs.

items.title: To start
items.text:
1. Create your account and sign in.
  2. Choose data: a file of your computer, or a file of the server.
  3. Generate the visualizations from the overview.

A problem: see Help. What changes in each version: What’s new.

items.title: Help
items.text: Message What to do “File outside the allowed folder” upload the file from the computer “Table no longer available” Connect in the message opens the Database tab again with its connection “Not enough numeric columns” choose another dataset, or more columns “Connection failed” check the server, the port, the database, the user and the password “The table already exists” (export) choose “Replace the table” or “Append the rows”, or another name The sign-in page shows the session has expired: sign in again The assistant says no model is set up the administrator of the server must turn it on (API key) “Address refused” (remote server, PACS) the server is on a private network: the administrator can allow it No code email (forgotten password) look in the spam folder; otherwise, the administrator checks the sending of emails

items.title: The assistant of the guide
items.text:
The round button at the bottom right of each page of this guide opens its assistant: ask a question in your own words.

  1. The button: open or close the assistant.
  2. The answer, taken from this guide.
  3. The pages where the guide talks about it: a click goes there.
  4. Your question (or one of the suggestions above).

The assistant only knows this guide: it sees neither your data nor your account. Depending on your server, it shows the passage of the guide that answers, or writes an answer from these passages; check the important points on the page given. The conversation follows from page to page, until the tab is closed.

items.title: Another problem
items.text: Write to the administrator of your Projecta server, giving the time, the screen and the message shown. If they ask for a request identifier, it is in the browser’s tools (X-Request-ID header).

items.title: Explore and export
items.text:
1. Four figures: rows, columns, duplicates, missing values.
  2. The table, page by page.
  3. Columns: the type and the missing values of each.
  4. Export to a file or a database.
  5. Generate the visualizations.
  6. The pages of the table.
Element Role Title full path of the dataset: folder, then file name (or engine and database, for a table) Chips format, size, loading state: at the end of the path, or under it when it fills the line Four figures rows, columns (numeric and text), duplicates, missing values Export, Change dataset, Generate the visualizations on the line of the figures, on the right Table all the rows, page by page Under the table rows per page (50, 100 or 200) on the left, pages in the centre (or a number to type), rows shown on the right Columns (side menu, under Overview) opens or closes the columns panel: type (number or text) and missing values of each

Empty cells are written empty. Numbers are aligned right.

items.title: Export
items.text:
Export (overview) writes the dataset on screen, with the loaded rows (a table: its first 10,000 rows), in another format or another database.

To a file: choose the format (CSV, TSV, Excel, Parquet, JSON or YAML), the file name and, for CSV, the separator (comma or semicolon). Then:

  • Download to this computer;
  • or Save on the server, in uploads/: the file then appears in “Choose data”; a name already taken gets “-1”.

To a database: choose the engine and the connection (filled with the last one of the workspace for each engine), the table name and what to do if it already exists: overwrite nothing (the export stops and says so), replace the table or append the rows. The “Columns created” table shows the name and the SQL type each column will get: lower case, no accents, _ instead of spaces. For SQLite, choose a database of the SQLite folder of the server, or New database… and its name (export.db).

items.title: Desktop app
items.text: Projecta also comes as a Windows application, with the same dashboard.

items.title: Download
items.text:
Download for Windows Portable version

Version 0.7.1, for Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit). Earlier versions and the SHA-256 checksums (SHA256SUMS.txt) are on the releases page. Once installed, the application updates itself (Help › Check for updates…).

File Use Projecta-Setup-<version>.exe installs it, with shortcuts on the desktop and in the Start menu Projecta-<version>-portable.exe runs without installation (a USB key, a computer without administrator rights)

“Windows protected your PC”

The application is not signed yet: on first launch, choose More info, then Run anyway.

This guide opens in the application with F1, in the language of the dashboard (Account › Language); the menus and windows of the application follow it too.

items.title: The server
items.text:
The application reads your data on Projecta online: nothing else to install, create your account on first launch. At startup, a Connecting to Projecta bar moves on until the server answers (after a pause, it takes a few seconds to wake up; the application waits up to 30 s for it). If it does not answer (no Internet), the Connection to Projecta failed screen says so, and a new try comes by itself (after 15 s, then 30 s, then every minute): nothing to do, your data stay on the server. Another server, for example the one of your department, is chosen in File › API address….

Demonstration data only

Projecta online is a shared server: send it only demonstration or already anonymized data, never real patient data.

items.title: Work without a connection
items.text:
When the connection to Projecta fails (no Internet, server stopped), the application goes on with what is on the computer:

  • What you opened stays readable: your workspaces, the datasets and the pages read, the visualizations, the studies opened (anonymized). A banner and the Offline · n changes waiting pill say so.
  • Your changes (the field or the columns of a workspace, the history, the measurements and the report of a study) wait for the reconnection; the pill opens their list, each can be cancelled.
  • A new try comes by itself (15 s, 30 s, then every minute). At the reconnection, the changes leave in order; if the same item also changed online meanwhile, the application asks which one to keep (for the measurements: both, if you wish).
  • Online only: loading a file, a database, the PACS, the assistant and new computations (visualizations, measurements of an ROI).
  • At startup without a connection, Continue offline opens what is kept.

What is kept is encrypted for your Windows account and erased at sign-out; after 7 days without a connection, you sign in again. Account › Settings › Offline: switch it on or off, keep the studies, the space on the disk, erase it all.

items.title: Open a file with Projecta
items.text:
Once installed, the application is added to the Open with menu of the Windows Explorer (right click on a file) for CSV, TSV, Excel, Parquet, JSON, YAML, DICOM (.dcm), NIfTI (.nii) files and the .zip files of studies. Always use this app makes it the application of that type (a double click is then enough).

  • A dataset is imported, then opened in the overview.
  • Medical images open Open medical images, the file already chosen: you decide on anonymization, then Open the exam.

If you are not signed in, the file waits for you to sign in. The portable version is not added to this menu (it installs nothing).

items.title: Send feedback
items.text:
Help › Send feedback… opens a small window to write to the team: a suggestion, a problem or a question.

  1. The kind: suggestion, problem or question.
  2. Your message.
  3. Attach the technical information (or not).

  4. Send.

  5. Choose the kind, write the message (what you were doing, what happened, what you expected).

  6. An address to answer you, if you wish (otherwise, the one of your account when you are signed in).
  7. Attach the technical information (ticked) adds the version, the system and the last lines of the log; See what is attached shows them before sending. Never a password or any data.
  8. Send.

If the server does not answer, the message is kept in the logs folder (avis-….txt): Open the folder to send it later.

items.title: Updates
items.text:
At startup (if the computer is online), Projecta checks whether a new version exists; a notification offers it: Later, or See and update. Help › Check for updates… does the same on request.

  1. Your version and the new one.
  2. What’s new in it.
  3. The download; the fingerprint of the file is checked before installing (a changed file is never installed).
  4. The settings: check at startup, download in the background.
  5. Restart and install: Projecta closes, installs, then starts again.

Nothing is forced: Later keeps your version. Your settings and the API address are kept. With the portable version, the new file is downloaded, then shown in its folder: replace the old one with it.

items.title: What differs from the browser
items.text:
• Exported files (charts, datasets, studies) are saved in Downloads\Projecta, without a question; a message gives their full path, with Open the folder. A name already taken gets a number: …_2D (2).png.
  • Help › Logs folder opens the folder of the main.log file (%APPDATA%\Projecta\logs on Windows): to attach to a request for help.
  • Account › What’s new says what changes from one version to the next.

items.title: Assistant
items.text:
The Assistant button, top right, opens a panel on the side of each screen. Ask a question about what you see: a dataset, visualizations, an imaging exam, a report.

  1. The Assistant button.
  2. What it sees of the open screen.
  3. A proposal: Apply or Ignore.
  4. Ready-made questions, and yours.

items.title: It proposes, you decide
items.text:
The assistant changes nothing by itself. When it suggests a setting, it shows it as a proposal, with Apply and Ignore:

Proposal What “Apply” does Columns to project chooses them for the visualizations, which are computed again Empty cells fills the given columns (mean, median, value) 2D view, 3D view or both changes how the visualizations are shown Draft of a report inserts it in the section (indication, technique, results); read it again, then save

It can neither export, nor delete, nor validate. It never writes the conclusion of a report: the diagnosis remains the physician’s.

When the dashboard is in English, the assistant answers in English.

items.title: What it sees
items.text:
At the top of the panel, a line says what the assistant sees of the open screen. By default:

  • the summary of the dataset on screen (columns, types, statistics, empty cells), not its rows;
  • for an exam: its code (anonymized), its information and your measurements, never the images nor the identity of the patient.

items.title: Settings and log
items.text:
The cog of the panel opens the settings of the workspace:

  • turn the assistant on or off in this workspace;
  • allow it to read 20 sample rows (off by default);
  • allow it to propose settings, to write drafts.

The log lists, for 30 days, each question, each reading, each proposal and what you did with it. CSV downloads it.

Answers to check

The assistant is a language model (Claude, by Anthropic): it can be wrong. Check the figures it quotes and read its drafts again. Your questions and the summary of the data are sent to this model by the Projecta server.

items.title: Account and sign-in
items.text:
1. Open the online dashboard, https://projecta-dash.vercel.app, or the desktop app, then Continue.
  2. The first time, Sign up: last name, first name, email address and password (at least 8 characters).
  3. Sign in with the address and the password. Without Remember me, the session lasts 30 minutes (JWT_EXPIRE_MINUTES).
  1. The email address of the account.
  2. The password (the eye shows it).
  3. Remember me: the session stays open 7 days.
  4. Forgot your password?: a code by email to choose another one.
  5. Google or GitHub, when set up on the server.
  6. Sign up: create an account.

Remember me keeps the session 7 days and the email address: the next time, the sign-in page fills it in (box ticked) and, if the session is still open, offers Open the dashboard or Switch account. The password is never kept by the application; the browser’s password manager may offer it.

When the session expires, the sign-in page says so: just sign in again.

items.title: With Google or GitHub
items.text:
If the administrator set it up, two round buttons show under Sign in and Sign up: Google and GitHub.

  1. Click one: the Google or GitHub page opens (in the desktop application, in your browser, which then asks to “open Projecta”).

  2. Sign in there and accept: the dashboard opens.

  3. First time with this address: an account is created, with the name given by Google or GitHub, without a password (you can set one in Profile).

  4. An account already exists with this address: you are signed in to it, and Google or GitHub is linked to it.

Projecta never receives your Google or GitHub password: only your name and your email address, if it is verified there. Remember me also counts for this sign-in.

items.title: Forgotten password
items.text:
1. On the sign-in page, Forgot your password?, then the address of the account and Send the code.
  2. A 6-digit code arrives by email; it is valid 15 minutes.
  3. Type the code and the new password (twice, at least 8 characters), then Change the password: the sign-in page opens, the address filled in.

A new code can be asked after a minute (Send the code again); it replaces the previous one. After 5 wrong codes, ask for a new one. The answer is the same for an address without an account.

No email?

Look in the spam folder. On a test server, emails may be held by the server instead of being sent: ask the administrator.

items.title: Account
items.text:
The round button with your initials, top right, opens the account menu.

Entry Content Profile first and last name (can be changed), email address, creation date; change of password (the current password is asked); Delete my account, after confirmation, with its workspaces and their history Language Français or English: the dashboard, the desktop application and this guide; kept for your account Settings rows per page, narrow side menu, “Columns” panel open when a dataset opens, visualizations shown; applied at once and kept in this browser; Restore the settings goes back to the defaults Notifications the messages of the session (uploads, errors, saves), newest first; the number of unread ones shows next to the entry Sign out closes the session; the token is revoked

items.title: Language
items.text: Account › Language: Français or English. The dashboard shows itself in that language at once, the desktop application (its menus and windows) follows it, and the book button opens this guide in it. The choice is kept for your account: it follows you on another computer. Data (file names, columns, exam descriptions, DICOM tag values) are never translated. In English, the names of the DICOM tags are those of the standard.

items.title: Linked accounts
items.text:
1. Identity: first and last name; the address does not change here.
  2. Password: change it, or set the first one.
  3. Linked accounts: Google and GitHub.
  4. Delete my account (after confirmation).

Profile › Linked accounts shows Google and GitHub: linked (with the address and the date) or not.

  • Link: the page of the provider opens; on return, a notification confirms. The address must be yours, or an address that has no Projecta account yet.
  • Unlink: after confirmation. Not possible if it is your only way to sign in: first set a password (Profile › Set a password, without a current password to give).

items.title: Load data
items.text: Choose data (side menu or home) opens a window with three tabs: Files, Database, Remote server.

items.title: A file
items.text:
1. The three tabs: Files, Database, Remote server.
  2. Search a file by its name.
  3. The files of the server, by folder.
  4. Drop a file of your computer (or Browse…).
  5. Load the chosen file.
Source How Server files sorted by folder; the search filters by name; choose a file, then Load (or double-click) From the computer drop a file in the frame, or Browse…; it is stored in uploads/ without replacing an existing file, then opens

Formats: CSV, TSV, Excel (.xls, .xlsx), Parquet, JSON and YAML, up to 100 MB. The separator, decimal commas (49,9) and the encoding are detected.

Each file is checked before it is kept: a file whose content does not match its extension (a program renamed .csv), an Excel workbook with macros, or a file made to overload the server is refused, with the reason.

items.title: A database table
items.text:
1. The engine: PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQLite.
  2. The database (for SQLite) or the server, database, user and password (for PostgreSQL and MySQL); here, also import a database from the computer.
  3. The tables of the database: choose one.

  4. Load its first rows.

  5. Database tab (or the “A database table” card of the home page).

  6. Choose the engine: PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQLite.
  7. PostgreSQL and MySQL: server, port, database, user, password (and schema for PostgreSQL), then Connect. SQLite: choose a database of the server, or Import a database from this computer… (a .db, .sqlite or .sqlite3 file, up to 200 MB), then Open.
  8. The tables show on the right; the search filters by name. Choose a table, then Load (or double-click): its first 10,000 rows are loaded.

The password is never saved: it stays in memory for the session. The other settings of a connection that worked fill the form the next time.

Each engine keeps its own values: going from PostgreSQL to MySQL shows the MySQL fields (empty the first time, with its port 3306), and going back to PostgreSQL finds what was typed for it.

If the connection fails, the reason shows instead of the tables (server unreachable, password refused…).

Your own databases: the PostgreSQL or MySQL server is given by its address, as the server of Projecta reaches it. Projecta online does not see the databases of your computer: only those open on the Internet. With a Projecta server on your computer, its own is called localhost. An SQLite database of your computer is imported (see above): it is copied to the server and stays in the list.

Tables to try

On a test server, the administrator can load sample data in the three databases: database app, schema public for PostgreSQL; app.db for SQLite.

items.title: A file from a remote server
items.text:
1. The source type: web link, S3 / MinIO or SFTP.
  2. The address of the file (or of the server).
  3. Test the link (or Connect, for S3 and SFTP).

Remote server tab, three source types:

Source Settings Then Web link http(s)://… address of the file; authentication: none, token (Bearer), user and password, or custom header (X-API-Key…); format, if the address has no extension Test the link shows the size and the first 5 rows, then Load S3 / MinIO endpoint (https://minio.lab.local:9000, s3.amazonaws.com), region, bucket, access key and secret key Connect, browse the folders, choose a file, Load SFTP server, port (22), user, password or private key (OpenSSH or PEM file, with its passphrase) the same

The Projecta server downloads the file (up to 100 MB) into uploads/remote/, checks it as an uploaded file, then opens it.

GitHub, Google Drive, Google Sheets, Dropbox

Paste the link as you copy it: Projecta turns it into a download link.

  • GitHub (page of a file, …/blob/main/data.csv): public repository, no authentication; private repository, authentication Token with a GitHub fine-grained token limited to this repository, permission Contents: Read-only (GitHub › Settings › Developer settings).
  • Google Drive (share link of a file): the file must be shared with "Anyone with the link".
  • Google Sheets: the open sheet is read as CSV (same sharing rule).
  • Dropbox: the share link.
  • Secrets: token, passwords, secret key and private key serve the current request, never saved. The other settings are kept in the workspace and fill the form the next time; kept links are offered under the address.
  • Download again at each opening: a link without authentication opened from the recent datasets is downloaded again (latest version, same file). If it does not answer, the version already downloaded opens.
  • SFTP: on the first connection, the fingerprint of the server (SHA256:…) is kept; if the server shows another one later, the connection is refused (like ssh).

Refused addresses

For safety, Projecta does not download from its own machine (localhost), nor, by default, from a private network (10.x, 192.168.x…). For a server of your laboratory’s network, ask the administrator to allow it.

items.title: Workspaces and history
items.text:
The Workspace: … button of the top bar opens the list of workspaces.

  1. The open workspace.
  2. The list: switch workspace, rename it, delete it; create one.
Action How Switch workspace click its name: the dataset it was working on opens again Create “New workspace”, a name, its field, Create Rename pencil Delete bin, then confirmation; the last workspace cannot be deleted

Each workspace keeps its dataset on screen, its recent datasets, its connections, its choice of columns and its way of filling empty cells. Deleting a workspace deletes its history, not the files nor the visualizations.

items.title: The field of a workspace
items.text:
Each workspace has its field: there, the dashboard puts first what you use most. At first launch, Projecta asks it with cards; Skip keeps the whole dashboard as it is.

Field What changes Medical imaging the IMAGING menu at the top, Open a study as the main button, the home page starts with the studies Clinical research the home page starts with the files (a cohort), then the tables Public health the home page starts with the database tables Data analysis the files and the tables, without imaging (menu and card hidden)

The assistant knows the field of the workspace and suggests, on the home page, questions that suit it. Another field: Account › Settings › Field of the workspace, or one workspace per field (“New workspace”). Nothing is removed: another field puts everything back in its place.

items.title: Recent datasets and history
items.text:
• The side menu shows the last 5 datasets of the workspace, the home page the last 3: a click opens them again.
  • Full history lists the last 10. The cross of a row removes it from the history (the file stays); Clear the history removes them all, after confirmation.

items.title: Medical imaging
items.text:
The IMAGING part of the side menu opens DICOM or NIfTI exams (MRI, CT…), shows them in three planes and in 3D, measures the lesions, follows their course from one exam to the next and prepares a report.

A help, not a diagnosis

Projecta helps reading and measuring. The diagnosis and the report remain the physician’s, who validates them. Projecta is not a certified medical device.

items.title: Try without patient data
items.text: The administrator can provide two synthetic MRIs of a fictional patient, six months apart (one lesion grows, one is stable, one is new), and a brain FDG PET-CT of the same patient (for the dose and the tags): no real data, enough to try every screen.

items.title: Open a study
items.text:
1. Files of the computer, PACS server or Recent studies.
  2. Drop the files or a folder (DICOM, NIfTI, .zip).
  3. Anonymize on opening (ticked by default).
  4. Open the exam.

Imaging › Studies › Open a study, three tabs:

Tab Content Files of the computer DICOM files (with or without the .dcm extension), a whole folder, .zip files, or NIfTI volumes (.nii, .nii.gz); up to 500 MB together PACS server a PACS reachable through DICOMweb (Orthanc, dcm4chee…): search by patient, dates and modality, choose the exam, then its series Recent studies the exams already opened

Anonymize on opening (ticked by default): the name, the full date of birth, the identifiers and the institution are removed from the working copy. The patient becomes a code (ANON-3F2A1C), the same for all their exams, so that they can be compared without knowing who it is. The code is computed with a secret of the server: without it, the identifier cannot be found again.

The original images do not change: Projecta works on a copy, visible to the user who opened it only, and which can be deleted from Studies.

A PACS of the hospital network

A PACS of the internal network must be allowed by the administrator (as remote servers are). The password or token of the PACS is not saved; its address is, in the workspace.

items.title: Viewer
items.text:
1. The exam: its anonymized code, its date; Export or share, Compare, Report.
  2. The tools: window, zoom, ruler, angle, ROI, Segment…
  3. The series of the exam.
  4. The axial slice; the sagittal and coronal slices next to it, the 3D rendering below.

  5. The slice slider.

  6. Series on the left; in the centre, the axial, sagittal and coronal slices (rebuilt from the volume: MPR) and a 3D rendering (maximum intensity projection, to rotate by dragging).

  7. A click places the crosshair: the two other planes show the slices through that point. The wheel, the slider under each view or the arrow keys scroll the slices.
  8. Tools: Window (drag: horizontally the width, vertically the centre), Zoom, Pan, Scroll, Ruler (drag from one point to the other), Angle (three clicks), ROI.
  9. Preset windows: “Auto” (the exam’s; in PET, from zero to the most avid voxels), and for CT: brain, soft tissue, lung, bone.
  10. The + button of a view adds it to the key images of the report; the enlarge button shows it alone.

items.title: Projections and PET/CT fusion
items.text:
The Display tab of the right panel sets how the planes are seen:

  • Projection: Slice (one slice), MIP (the highest value over the thickness: PET foci, injected vessels), MinIP (the lowest: bronchi, emphysema) or Mean (smooths the noise), over a thickness of 5 to 100 mm or the whole volume.
  • PET / CT fusion (also the Fusion button of the toolbar, for a study with a PET and a CT): the PET in colours over the CT, its opacity, its colours (hot, rainbow, grey) and its window. The two series of a study are lined up by their DICOM coordinates. The 3D view then shows the MIP of the PET in inverted grey; ▶ turns it.
  • Under the crosshair: the value of the CT (HU) and the one of the PET, in SUV when the series gives its unit (Bq/mL), the patient's weight and the injected dose; with the SUVmax and SUVmean of a 1 cm sphere.

items.title: On a tablet
items.text:
On a tablet (in landscape) or a narrow window, the viewer shows one large view, to read an exam again at the bedside or in a meeting: the same dashboard, in the browser, nothing to install.

  1. The large view (axial; the enlarge button shows the four views).
  2. The series, on the right.
  3. The tools, as 64 px buttons: Scroll, Window, Zoom, Ruler, ROI.
  4. Cine: the slices go by on their own; a second press stops them.
Gesture Effect Drag one finger (Scroll) the slices go by Long press, then drag the window (drag right: wider; up: brighter) Two fingers zoom (spread, pinch) and pan Tap the crosshair goes there

With another tool chosen, the finger does what the tool does (window, zoom, ruler, ROI). The arrow top left goes back to the studies. Segmentation, export, sharing and the report stay on the computer.

15 minutes

On a tablet, the session closes after 15 minutes without touching the screen: a tablet is easily lent. Sign in again to go on.

items.title: DICOM tags and dose
items.text:
1. The Tags tab of the right panel, which widens.
  2. Search a tag: by number, name or value.
  3. The filters: All, Patient, Exam, Image, Removed or replaced.
  4. The On opening column: what anonymization did to the tag.
  5. CSV: the full list, to attach to a request or to compare.

The Tags tab lists every public tag of the first image of the series (the private tags of manufacturers and the pixels are not kept). Those of a sequence follow the sequence, marked ›. In English, the names of the tags are those of the DICOM standard; their values are never translated.

On opening Meaning Kept the value of the file Replaced the name and the identifier of the patient, replaced by their code Removed an identity item (date of birth, institution, physicians, accession number, UIDs…): its value was not kept

An exam opened without anonymization keeps all its values. Exams opened before this version only show the summary of the settings: open the files again to see every tag.

  1. Dose of this exam, at the bottom of the Information tab.
  2. The CT: CTDIvol and DLP.
  3. The PET: tracer, activity, time of injection.
  4. The estimated effective dose of the exam.

Dose of this exam (Information tab), when the headers give it:

  • CT: the mean CTDIvol of the slices and the DLP (dose-length product: CTDIvol × length covered);
  • PET or scintigraphy: the tracer, the injected activity (MBq) and the time of injection;
  • estimated effective dose (mSv): DLP × a coefficient of the region examined (head 0.0021; neck 0.0059; chest 0.014; abdomen and pelvis 0.015), plus, for FDG, 0.019 mSv per MBq;
  • Follow-up · this patient, 12 months: their exams of the twelve previous months opened in Projecta, and their total.

An estimate

The effective dose is an adult estimate from published coefficients, not a dosimetry of the patient. When an exam has several CT series (reconstructions), the one with the highest DLP is counted once. Other tracers than FDG have no estimate.

items.title: Measurements and analysis
items.text:
An ROI is an ellipse drawn around a lesion. The view zooms on the part drawn to look at it closely (a click on the name of the ROI, in Measurements, goes back to it; Reset shows the whole image again). At the top of Measurements, the Regions gallery shows each region drawn on the series, with its volume; it grows with each new ROI, and a click on a thumbnail goes back to it. The API computes:

  • on the slice: area, mean ± standard deviation, minimum and maximum;
  • the lesion: the voxels brighter than half-way between the peak of the ellipse and the tissue at its edge (“half-maximum” outline), connected to the peak, on the slice and the neighbouring slices; its volume and the number of slices it covers;
  • 18 radiomic features: shape (volume, surface, sphericity, elongation, largest diameter), intensity (mean, standard deviation, median, 10th and 90th percentiles, skewness, kurtosis, entropy, uniformity), texture (contrast, homogeneity, correlation and energy of the co-occurrence matrix).

The half-maximum outline suits lesions clearly brighter than the tissue around (FLAIR hyperintensities, contrast uptake). For a dark or poorly outlined lesion, check the volume.

The measurements are saved with the exam. Measurements as CSV downloads them.

Add to the cohort adds the lesion, one row per lesion, to a dataset (imagerie/cohortes/<name>.csv of the datasets folder): patient code, date of the exam, series, name of the lesion, sex, age and the 18 features. Once loaded, the cohort is projected like any dataset (PCA, t-SNE, UMAP): lesions that look alike group together.

items.title: Segment the lesions
items.text:
The Segment tool proposes the outline of the lesions, in 3D; you correct it, then validate it.

  1. The Segment tool: the right panel becomes the segmentation panel.
  2. The way to segment: Click, Threshold, Brush, Eraser.
  3. Its setting: the tolerance (Click), the threshold (Threshold) or the radius of the brush.
  4. The lesions: name, slices, volume (mL). A click chooses a lesion (its name can be changed); the bin removes it.
  5. The 3D rendering shows the lesions in colour.
  6. The slices of the chosen lesion: a click goes there.
Way What it does Click a click in the lesion: the connected voxels of close value (± the tolerance, a share of the width of the window shown) are proposed, on the slice or, with Follow on the neighbouring slices, in 3D Threshold the same, with the voxels above a value Brush dragging on a slice adds a disc to the chosen lesion (a new one if there is none) Eraser dragging removes from the chosen lesion (from all, without a chosen lesion)

A proposal that would cover more than 5 % of the volume is refused: the tolerance spills over the tissue around; lower it, or raise the threshold.

Validate keeps the lesions with the exam, with their volume and the 18 radiomic features (as an ROI); Cancel goes back to the validated lesions. Once validated:

  • Add to the cohort: one row per lesion in the cohort’s dataset (see Measurements and analysis);
  • NIfTI mask: a .nii.gz file where each lesion has its number (1, 2, 3…), aligned with the export of the volume: for 3D Slicer, ITK-SNAP or Python.

A help to outline

The proposal follows the values of the image, not the anatomy: check each slice, correct with the brush and the eraser. Nothing is kept without Validate.

items.title: Compare two exams
items.text:
Compare shows the same series of two exams of the same patient, side by side:

  • Linked scrolling: both views scroll together;
  • Automatic alignment: the slices are paired by the position of the head (the centre of the patient in each volume), which makes up for a patient placed higher or lower. It is not a full registration (rotation, deformation);
  • Course of the lesions: the ROIs of the same name in both exams, with their volume and the change (+12 %, new, gone), and the chart of the volume of each lesion across all the exams.

To follow a lesion, give it the same name in each exam (“Lesion” field of the measurement).

items.title: Report
items.text:
A draft is filled in: indication, technique (sequences, field), results (each lesion and its course compared with the previous exam), conclusion to write. The key images and the measurements are attached.

  • Save the draft;
  • Export to PDF: the print window of the browser, the report alone;
  • Validate: a conclusion and a signature are needed; the report can no longer be changed, unless you Reopen the draft.

Sending to the PACS (DICOM SR) is planned for a next version.

items.title: Export or share
items.text:
Export or share (top of the viewer):

  1. The format of the export.
  2. For the video: the speed and the size of the images.
  3. What is burnt into the images.
  4. For whom?: a name, to find your way among your links.
  5. The duration of the link, the access code, then Create the link.
  6. The link to copy, and the code to send separately (another message).
  7. The export button, depending on the format chosen.
Export Content The view shown (PNG) the enlarged view (otherwise the axial one), at the slice and with the window of the screen, 2,048 px wide The cine as a video every slice of that plane, at 5, 10 or 20 images per second; MP4, or WebM if the browser cannot write MP4 The images of the series (JPEG, .zip) one image per slice The anonymized DICOM series (.zip) DICOM images written anew, for another software or a colleague The volume (NIfTI, .nii.gz) for analysis (Python, 3D Slicer…)

The exports carry what the exam kept at its opening: an anonymized exam stays anonymized (the patient code, never their name). The burnt-in items (measurements, exam code, date and series, 1 cm scale bar) are ticked for the images and the video.

Share a link: the person who gets it opens the exam in a read only viewer, without an account (window, zoom, pan, scroll; neither measurement nor download):

  1. Read only.
  2. The end date of the link.

  3. The reading tools and the window.

  4. Duration: 24 hours, 7 days or 30 days. An expired link no longer opens anything and leaves the list.

  5. Access code (advised): 6 digits, shown once, to send by another way than the link. After 10 wrong codes, the link is locked.
  6. Active links: for whom, end date, number of openings. Revoke cuts the link at once.
  7. Only an anonymized exam can be shared. Deleting the exam also cuts its links.

A link is a key

Whoever has the link (and its code) sees the exam until its end date. Prefer the access code, the shortest useful duration, and revoke a link that is no longer of use.

items.title: Formats read
items.text:
Format Remarks DICOM one image per file (multi-frame files are not read yet), sorted by position; series grouped by SeriesInstanceUID, exams by StudyInstanceUID NIfTI-1 .nii or .nii.gz; a 4D volume shows its first volume

The volumes are reoriented for radiological reading (the patient’s right on the left of the screen, the front at the top). Beyond 48 million voxels, the in-plane resolution is halved.

items.title: What’s new
items.text:
What changes from one version to the next. In the application, Account › What’s new shows the same thing.

  1. The version you use.
  2. What it brought (open); the previous versions below.

Written in French

The change log of Projecta is written in French, as below.

items.title: Modifié

items.title: Corrigé
items.text: • Application de bureau : après la connexion avec Google ou GitHub dans le navigateur, l’application ouvre le tableau de bord ; elle restait sur la page de connexion.

items.title: Ajouté
items.text:
• Pages de connexion, d’inscription et de mot de passe oublié sur tablette (Projecta à gauche, le formulaire à droite) et sur téléphone (une colonne ; créer un compte commence par Google et GitHub) : le nom de chaque champ au-dessus de lui, Google et GitHub avec leur nom.
  • Le domaine d’un espace de travail (imagerie médicale, recherche clinique, santé publique, analyse de données) : demandé une fois avec des cartes, choisi à la création d’un espace, changé dans Compte › Paramètres ; le menu, le bouton principal, l’accueil et les suggestions de l’assistant suivent. La version lancée depuis le projet ajoute la géomatique (SIG).
  • Imagerie, onglet Affichage (maquette 32) : chaque plan en coupe ou en projection sur une épaisseur (MIP, MinIP, moyenne) ; la fusion TEP/TDM (bouton Fusion) : la TEP en couleurs sur la TDM, alignée par les coordonnées DICOM, son opacité, ses couleurs, sa fenêtre en SUV, la MIP de la TEP qui tourne, et sous la croix la valeur, le SUVmax et le SUVmoy.
  • Application de bureau : travailler sans connexion (maquettes 68 à 72). Ce qui a été ouvert reste lisible, chiffré sur l’ordinateur ; les changements attendent la reconnexion (pastille « Hors ligne · n changements en attente », liste annulable) et partent d’eux-mêmes, un même élément changé en ligne entre-temps demandant lequel garder ; « Continuer hors ligne » au démarrage ; Compte › Paramètres › Hors ligne.

items.title: Modifié
items.text:

  • Sites de documentation : plus de bandeau « Made with Zensical » en bas des pages ; la page d’une adresse qui ne mène nulle part (404) tient sur un écran, sans défiler.

items.title: Corrigé
items.text:

  • Les listes déroulantes (domaine, taille des pages, fenêtre de l’imagerie…) prennent la police du tableau de bord.
  • Le lien du tableau de bord en ligne (guide, Nouveautés) mène au bon site, https://projecta-dash.vercel.app : l’adresse projecta-dashboard.vercel.app appartient à un autre compte Vercel.

items.title: Sécurité
items.text: • Bibliothèques mises à jour pour des failles connues : certifi, requests, python-dotenv et scikit-learn (1.5.2).

items.title: Ajouté
items.text:
• Imagerie : la galerie Régions, en tête de Mesures : chaque région tracée (ROI) en vignette, avec son volume, complétée à chaque nouvelle ROI ; un clic y revient.
  • Application de bureau : elle s’ajoute au menu Ouvrir avec de Windows pour les fichiers CSV, TSV, Excel, Parquet, JSON, YAML, DICOM, NIfTI et les .zip d’examens ; un jeu s’ouvre dans l’aperçu, des images dans « Ouvrir des images médicales ».
  • Documentation : les sites d’administration et de développement sur Vercel, pour l’équipe seulement, et la référence de l’API publique (projecta-api).

items.title: Modifié
items.text:

  • Guide de l’utilisateur : la connexion passe par le tableau de bord en ligne, https://projecta-dash.vercel.app (ou l’application de bureau), au lieu d’une adresse locale.

items.title: Corrigé
items.text: • Connexion avec Google ou GitHub : une adresse de retour complète collée dans OAUTH_API_URL (« …/api/v1/auth/oauth/…/callback ») ne fait plus refuser la connexion par Google ; seule la base de l’API compte.

items.title: Ajouté
items.text:
• Guide de l’utilisateur : Télécharger pour Windows (l’installateur, et la version portable) sur l’accueil et la page de l’application de bureau.
  • Serveur : REDIS_URL pour un Redis hébergé (connexion chiffrée rediss://), comme celui de l’intégration Redis Cloud de FastAPI Cloud, et DATASET_CACHE_HOURS pour la durée d’un jeu chargé dans Redis. Une page de l’administration dit comment héberger l’API sur FastAPI Cloud, pour se connecter sans Docker.
  • Imagerie : la vue zoome sur la ROI tracée pour la regarder de près ; un clic sur son nom, dans Mesures, y revient.
  • Tableau de bord : une page 404 pour une adresse fausse ou ancienne (retour à l’accueil, ou choisir des données).
  • Documentation : une page 404 sur chaque site, avec la recherche et les premières pages.
  • API : /docs aux couleurs de Projecta (logo, liens, santé de l’API) et /reference, une référence en trois colonnes avec des exemples de code.
  • Le tableau de bord en ligne, en https (Vercel) ; l’application de bureau et le tableau de bord utilisent l’API en ligne par défaut : plus besoin de Docker pour essayer Projecta.
  • Le tableau de bord sur tablette (tout, à la taille du doigt) et sur téléphone, pour consulter : jeux récents, examens, aperçu et visualisation en deux onglets, visionneuse plan par plan, examens partagés.

items.title: Modifié
items.text:
• Le guide de l’utilisateur est publié seulement sur GitHub Pages : https://adama-r.github.io/Projecta/.
  • Application de bureau : elle attend jusqu’à 30 s qu’une API en ligne réponde (elle se réveille après une pause).
  • Licence : Projecta est gratuit à utiliser pour l’essayer, tous droits réservés (plus de licence MIT).

items.title: Ajouté
items.text:
• Assistant (bouton en haut à droite) : il répond sur l’écran ouvert et propose des colonnes, le traitement des cases vides, la vue 2D ou 3D, un brouillon de compte rendu ; rien ne change sans « Appliquer ». Réglages et journal (30 jours) par espace de travail ; jamais les images ni l’identité des patients. Il s’active avec une clé de l’API Anthropic.
  • Accueil : une carte « Des images médicales ».
  • make local : Redis seul dans Docker, l’API et le tableau de bord sur la machine.
  • Documentation en trois sites : le guide de l’utilisateur (public, aussi dans l’application de bureau), l’administration et le développement (internes) ; pages sur la configuration, la sécurité, l’assistant, l’imagerie, l’hébergement (Vercel, Cloudflare), les comptes du projet, MCP et n8n.
  • CLAUDE.md et AGENTS.md : le projet expliqué aux assistants de code.
  • Documentation : des captures d’écran avec des repères numérotés, et ce que montre chaque numéro, sur les pages des trois guides.
  • Application de bureau : Aide › Envoyer un avis… (suggestion, problème ou question), avec les informations techniques si vous le voulez ; gardé sur l’ordinateur si le serveur ne répond pas.
  • Se connecter avec Google ou GitHub (boutons ronds sous le formulaire, s’ils sont configurés) : le compte est créé, ou relié à celui de la même adresse vérifiée. Profil › Comptes reliés pour relier ou délier ; un compte créé ainsi peut définir un mot de passe. Dans l’application de bureau, la page de Google ou GitHub s’ouvre dans le navigateur, puis revient à l’application.
  • Imagerie, onglet Balises : toutes les balises DICOM de la série, avec une recherche, des filtres (patient, examen, image, retirées ou remplacées), ce que l’anonymisation a fait de chacune et un export CSV.
  • Imagerie, Dose de cet examen (onglet Informations) : CTDIvol et PDL du scanner, traceur et activité de la TEP, dose efficace estimée, et le cumul des examens du patient sur 12 mois.
  • Une TEP-TDM de synthèse s’ajoute aux examens d’essai.
  • Imagerie, Exporter ou partager : la vue affichée (PNG), le ciné en vidéo, les images de la série (JPEG), la série DICOM anonymisée, le volume NIfTI ; mesures, code de l’examen et barre d’échelle incrustés au choix.
  • Imagerie, Segmenter : un clic dans une lésion propose son contour en 3D (croissance de région), ou au-dessus d’un seuil ; pinceau et gomme pour corriger ; volume de chaque lésion, rendu 3D en couleur ; « Valider » garde les lésions et leurs caractéristiques, à ajouter à une cohorte ou à exporter en masque NIfTI.
  • Documentation : un assistant sur chacun des trois sites (bouton en bas à droite) : il trouve dans le site le passage qui répond, avec ses liens ; si l’administrateur l’active, il rédige la réponse à partir de ces passages. Les secrets collés sont masqués avant l’envoi.
  • Application de bureau : mises à jour. Au démarrage, une notification propose la nouvelle version ; Aide › Rechercher des mises à jour… montre ses nouveautés, la télécharge, vérifie son empreinte, puis « Redémarrer et installer ». Jamais forcée.
  • Imagerie sur tablette : une grande vue, les séries à droite, des boutons pour le doigt ; glisser fait défiler les coupes, deux doigts zooment, un appui long règle la fenêtre ; « Ciné » fait défiler les coupes. La session se ferme après 15 minutes sans activité.
  • Imagerie, liens de partage : un examen anonymisé s’ouvre en lecture seule, sans compte, pendant 24 heures, 7 ou 30 jours, avec un code d’accès à envoyer à part ; liste des liens actifs, nombre d’ouvertures, révocation.
  • English : menu du compte › Langue (Français ou English). Le tableau de bord, l’application de bureau (menus et fenêtres) et les réponses de l’assistant passent en anglais ; le choix est gardé dans le compte. Les données, elles, ne sont jamais traduites, et ce journal reste en français.
  • Le guide de l’utilisateur en anglais (menu de langue en haut de chaque page, qui ouvre la même page dans l’autre langue), avec ses captures et son assistant.
  • Visualisations, Exporter : HTML, PNG, SVG, PDF, JPEG ou WebP. Les images sont dessinées par le navigateur : elles marchent avec ou sans Docker, et dans l’application de bureau.
  • Les fichiers chargés sont vérifiés avant d’être gardés : contenu conforme à l’extension, pas de macros Excel, pas de fichier fait pour saturer le serveur ; refusés avec la raison. À l’export (CSV, Excel), une cellule qui commencerait une formule (=, +, -, @) reste du texte.
  • Serveur distant : un lien GitHub (dépôt privé : avec un jeton), Google Drive, Google Sheets ou Dropbox collé tel quel est téléchargé.
  • Assistant : Ollama au choix de Claude, gratuit (Ollama Cloud, avec des limites d’usage) ou sur votre machine ; les réglages de l’assistant disent quel modèle répond.
  • Documentation : flèches « page précédente / suivante » en bas de chaque page, police de la documentation de FastAPI (Roboto) ; sur le site de développement, la référence du code, écrite à partir des docstrings (que son assistant lit aussi).
  • /docs et /redoc de l’API portent le logo de Projecta ; chaque groupe de routes y est décrit (backend/metadata.py).

items.title: Modifié
items.text:
• Redis : l’API se connecte avec son propre utilisateur, limité aux clés de Projecta ; l’utilisateur default est désactivé ; un utilisateur admin pour la maintenance.
  • Documentation construite avec Zensical (à la place de MkDocs).
  • Logfire : métriques du processeur et de la mémoire.
  • En-tête commun à tous les fichiers Python.
  • Nouveau logo : trois plans de coupe empilés et les points d’une projection ; icônes de l’onglet, de l’application de bureau et de la documentation ; sous-titre « Données et imagerie ».
  • E-mails : envoi possible sans compte Gmail (Brevo, gratuit) ; adresse de réponse SMTP_REPLY_TO (avec un expéditeur « noreply »).
  • Pages de connexion, d’inscription et de mot de passe oublié : chaque bloc a sa place (plus rien ne se chevauche) ; une seule erreur, lisible, au-dessus du bouton, au lieu de deux petites lignes rouges.
  • Exporter vers une base de données : les trois choix « Si la table existe déjà » tiennent sur une ligne, avec une phrase qui dit ce que fait le choix ; la liste « Colonnes créées » est plus haute.
  • /api/v1 répond (nom, version, liens vers la documentation et la santé de l’API) au lieu d’une erreur 404.
  • Le menu latéral est réduit à ses icônes ; le pointeur sur son bouton l’ouvre par-dessus la page, un clic le garde ouvert (comme dans l’application Claude).
  • Visualisations : la ligne d’origine d’un point s’affiche quand on le clique, plus au survol (les étiquettes s’empilaient).
  • Aperçu : l’en-tête tient sur deux lignes (chemin et puces, puis chiffres et boutons) ; le tableau montre plus de lignes. Marges de la page réduites (10 px en haut, 20 px sur les côtés).
  • Sécurité : dépendances mises à jour (FastAPI 0.143 et Starlette 1.8, python-multipart, cryptography, urllib3, anyio, aiomysql, Vite…) ; les jetons de connexion sont signés avec PyJWT à la place de python-jose, qui n’a plus de correctif. L’image Docker de l’API est à reconstruire.

items.title: Corrigé
items.text:
• La connexion échouait (en local et dans Docker) : l’utilisateur Redis donné dans .env n’existait pas, et l’image Docker de l’API ne contenait pas les nouvelles dépendances.
  • Les tests passent sans fichier .env (comme dans GitHub Actions).
  • Pile Docker : le tableau de bord ne se chargeait plus (seul le bouton de la documentation marchait), faute du journal des versions ; il s’ouvre désormais même sans ce fichier.
  • Le mot « null » ne s’affiche plus dans un message d’erreur sans conseil, dans la liste des bases SQLite ni dans la fenêtre des cases vides.
  • Le guide de l’utilisateur se publie de nouveau sur Vercel (son Python refusait pip install), en français et en anglais.
  • L’API se déploie sur FastAPI Cloud : il lui manquait fastapi[standard] (la commande fastapi run).

items.title: Ajouté
items.text:
• Le projet s’appelle désormais Projecta : tableau de bord, application de bureau, documentation, installateur Windows.
  • CHANGELOG.md, RELEASE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, modèles d’issues et de pull requests, mises à jour automatiques des dépendances (Dependabot).
  • Compte › Nouveautés : ce journal dans le tableau de bord, la version en cours ouverte ; après une mise à jour, une notification le propose une fois.
  • Serveur distant (onglet de « Choisir des données ») : charger un fichier d’un lien web (sans authentification, jeton, utilisateur et mot de passe, ou en-tête), d’un stockage S3 / MinIO ou d’un serveur SFTP (mot de passe ou clé privée), avec les dossiers à parcourir et l’aperçu des premières lignes. Les liens et serveurs sont gardés dans l’espace de travail, sans leurs secrets ; un lien peut être téléchargé de nouveau à chaque ouverture.
  • Imagerie médicale (menu IMAGERIE) : ouvrir des examens DICOM (fichiers, dossier, .zip) ou NIfTI, ou les séries d’un PACS en DICOMweb, anonymisés par défaut (le patient devient un code, le même pour tous ses examens) ; visionneuse en trois plans (MPR) et rendu 3D, fenêtrage, zoom, règle, angle, ROI ; volume des lésions et 18 caractéristiques radiomiques ; cohortes de lésions projetées comme un jeu de données ; comparaison de deux examens avec l’évolution des lésions ; compte rendu (brouillon, images clés, export PDF, validation). make imaging-demo écrit des IRM de synthèse pour essayer.
  • Journaux et télémétrie : une ligne par requête (route, statut, durée, utilisateur) avec un identifiant X-Request-ID ; événements d’usage (connexion, chargement, export, visualisation) ; traces Logfire de l’API (SQL, Redis, HTTP) quand un jeton est donné ; erreurs du tableau de bord envoyées à l’API ; journal main.log de l’application de bureau (Aide › Dossier des journaux). Paramètres › Statistiques d’utilisation coupe les statistiques de navigation.
  • Redis : un utilisateur dédié (ACL) avec REDIS_USERNAME.
  • Documentation : vue d’ensemble du projet en schémas (composants, fonctions, déploiement, CI, évolution), guide de l’imagerie, publication sur GitHub Pages et suivi des Actions avec gh, proposition de connexion avec Google et GitHub.

items.title: Modifié
items.text:
• E-mails : make mail-test TO=… envoie un e-mail de test avec les réglages SMTP_* ; port 465 (SMTP_SSL) ; le certificat du serveur est vérifié ; nouvelle page « E-mails » de la documentation (Mailpit, Gmail).
  • Visualisations : titre, nom du jeu et réglages sur une ligne, puces plus petites, explication de la méthode derrière un bouton « i » ; les graphiques tiennent sans défilement sur un écran 1 920 × 1 080 à 125 %.
  • Pages de bienvenue et de connexion : sans défilement jusqu’à une fenêtre de 1 280 × 600.
  • Bouton « Choisir des données » du menu latéral un peu plus grand.
  • Workflows GitHub Actions : chaque action est épinglée sur un commit (avec sa version en commentaire) ; mots de passe de la CI générés à chaque exécution ; publication de l’application de bureau sans paramètre saisi à la main ; documentation publiée aussi depuis trunk.

items.title: Sécurité
items.text:
• Imagerie : les examens ouverts (copies de travail) et les cohortes ne sont jamais suivis par Git ; chaque examen n’est visible que de l’utilisateur qui l’a ouvert.
  • Serveur distant : l’API refuse de télécharger depuis sa propre machine, les adresses réservées et, par défaut, les réseaux privés (REMOTE_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORKS) ; l’authentification d’un lien n’est pas transmise à un autre serveur lors d’une redirection ; la clé d’un serveur SFTP est vérifiée à chaque connexion.

items.title: Ajouté
items.text:
• Exporter un jeu chargé vers un fichier (CSV, TSV, Excel, Parquet, JSON, YAML), téléchargé ou rangé sur le serveur, ou vers une table PostgreSQL, MySQL ou SQLite, avec l’aperçu des colonnes créées.
  • Cases vides : avant de générer les visualisations, choisir comment compléter les cases vides des colonnes numériques (moyenne, médiane, zéro, valeur fixe), avec le nombre de lignes dessinées.
  • Mot de passe oublié : code à 6 chiffres envoyé par e-mail (Mailpit dans la pile Docker), valable 15 minutes.
  • Se souvenir de moi : session de 7 jours, adresse remplie à la connexion suivante, session encore ouverte proposée.
  • Vos propres bases : localhost désigne votre ordinateur même quand l’API tourne dans Docker ; import d’une base SQLite de l’ordinateur.
  • Application de bureau (Electron) : make desktop, installateur et version portable pour Windows (make desktop-exe), adresse de l’API réglable, publication par GitHub Release.
  • make dev : API (données en mémoire), tableau de bord et documentation, sans Docker, en une commande.
  • Logo : favicons, tableau de bord, pages de connexion, documentation, icônes de l’application de bureau.
  • Chaque moteur de base de données garde ses propres valeurs dans le formulaire de connexion.

items.title: Modifié
items.text:
• Pages de bienvenue et de connexion : fond du tableau de bord, titre du formulaire centré.
  • Aperçu : chemin complet du jeu sur toute la largeur, boutons alignés avec les informations du fichier ; pagination centrée sous le tableau.

items.title: Corrigé
items.text:
• Le formulaire de connexion à une base ne passe plus sous le pied de la fenêtre sur un écran 1 920 × 1 080 à 125 %.
  • Les vues 3D s’affichent dans l’application de bureau sans processeur graphique (WSLg).
Première version utilisable, après la migration vers une architecture hexagonale.

items.title: Ajouté
items.text:
• API FastAPI sous /api/v1 : comptes et connexion (JWT), espaces de travail et historique (Redis), jeux de données (fichiers et tables PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite), visualisations 2D et 3D (PCA, t-SNE, UMAP choisi automatiquement).
  • Tableau de bord (Vite) : accueil, choix des données, aperçu page par page, colonnes, visualisations Plotly, espaces de travail.
  • Lecture des CSV (séparateur, virgules décimales et encodage détectés), Excel, Parquet, JSON et YAML ; import depuis l’ordinateur.
  • Pile Docker Compose (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Redis, API, tableau de bord, documentation) et make seed pour les données d’exemple.
  • Tests : unitaires, d’intégration, contre les vrais serveurs, et dans le navigateur (Playwright) ; CI GitHub Actions.

items.title: Sécurité
items.text: • Secrets retirés du dépôt ; mots de passe exigés pour PostgreSQL et Redis ; accès aux fichiers limité au dossier des jeux de données.

items.title: Visualize
items.text:
Generate the visualizations reduces the numeric columns to two or three components and draws them.

  1. Columns: those projected (here 8 of 8).
  2. The 2D view: clicking a point shows its original row.
  3. The 3D view: drag to rotate it, wheel to zoom.

items.title: Empty cells
items.text:
If cells of the numeric columns to reduce are empty, a window first asks how to fill them, column by column:

Choice The empty cells get Leave empty (default) nothing: incomplete rows are not drawn Mean, Median the mean or the median of the other cells of the column Zero, Fixed value… 0, or the value typed

“For all the columns” applies a choice to each one; the bottom of the window says how many rows will be drawn. Leave all by default generates without filling anything. The dataset itself is never changed.

With Keep these choices ticked, they are kept in the workspace for this dataset: the question is not asked again, and the Missing values button of the visualizations changes them (the views are then generated again). Opening another dataset starts from the default settings.

items.title: View settings
items.text:
• Method: chosen automatically (PCA, t-SNE or UMAP) from the size of the dataset and the correlations; the chip shows it.
  • Columns: choose the numeric columns to reduce (all by default; at least 2, 3 for 3D), then Apply. The choice is kept in the workspace.
  • Missing values: change how the empty cells are filled (greyed out if the reduced columns have none).
  • 2D / 3D / Both: the views shown.
  • Click a point: the values of its original row, in a small box (one at a time; Escape or × closes it). Nothing shows on hover.
  • 3D: drag to rotate, wheel to zoom.
  • Export (down arrow): the view as HTML (interactive), PNG, SVG (vector), PDF (one page), JPEG or WebP. The images are drawn by the browser, on the background of the dashboard: with or without Docker, and in the desktop application. A message says where the file is: in a browser, its downloads folder (Ctrl+J shows it); in the desktop application, the full path in Downloads\Projecta, with Open the folder.
  • Enlarge (four corners): the view in full screen; Shrink, top right, or the Esc key brings it back.
  • Generate again: compute again after a change.

Beyond 5,000 rows, 5,000 random points are shown. A dataset with fewer than two numeric columns cannot be visualized.
